title: NDT Inspection
summary: The hovering aerial manipulator starts outside a large warehouse building, facing one of its long walls, and high up on that wall a small rectangle is marked out with yellow-and-black hazard tape. Carry out a non-destructive-testing style inspection: bring the end effector to the fixed inspection point in front of the marked rectangle (see the goal geometry) and keep it there for 100 consecutive control steps (0.83 s).
scene: The ground is the world's z = 0 plane. The scene is NVIDIA's static sample warehouse (shelving racks, pallets, boxes, signs, a forklift and a posed worker figure, none of which moves). The robot hovers a short distance in front of the outer face of one of the building's long walls, which faces it squarely. That wall is a flat, solid panel surface from a few metres above the ground up to the roof; below it the building is open, so at the robot's height the warehouse interior, a pillar on either side and a few signs in the wall's plane are visible. Straight ahead of the robot and well above it, a marked region is taped onto the wall: a rectangle of yellow-and-black hazard-striped reflective tape 3 cm wide, 0.30 m tall and 0.22 m wide outside (0.24 x 0.16 m inside). The tape is visual only (no collision). Far off to the robot's right stands a separate concrete wall slab (0.1 x 2 x 2 m) that plays no part in the task. Nothing moves and nothing varies between instances. The robot starts hovering level and motionless, facing the warehouse wall, with its arm at its zero joint configuration (end effector a little ahead of and above the airframe) and the gripper closed.
scene_privileged: One environment; its origin is the world origin. Robot at every reset: base_link at (0, 0, 1.0) m with orientation (1, 0, 0, 0) wxyz (body +x is the world +x direction), zero velocity; arm_link1_pitch_joint = arm_link2_pitch_joint = arm_link3_pitch_joint = arm_link4_roll_joint = 0 rad; arm_lfinger_joint = arm_rfinger_joint = 0.001 m (their lower limit: gripper closed, gripper_width 0.002 m). By the robot's URDF kinematics this puts ee_link at about (0.227, 0, 1.124) m with identity orientation and the tool-tip point (ee_link origin + 0.18 m along the ee_link x axis) at about (0.407, 0, 1.124) m; the end-effector command is initialised to the current ee_link pose. Warehouse: Isaac Sim's sample scene Samples/Replicator/Benchmark/full_warehouse_worker_benchmark_sdg.usd, loaded from NVIDIA's asset server (Isaac 5.1 asset root) together with the Simple_Warehouse props, materials and textures, the Reallusion worker character and the forklift it references; translated by (28.3, 0, 0) m, unrotated; static colliders only, no rigid bodies. Its wall facing the robot is the plane x = 1.97 m (interior x > 1.97, y from -23.4 to 30.6 m); between pillars at y = -2.4 and 3.6 m (0.55 m wide, front at x = 1.87) it consists of single-quad panels with mesh collision from z = 3 to 9 m; the panels of the band z 0..3 m are authored at 1/100 scale in this asset, so that band is open. Roof at z = 9 m. Marker: marked_region.usda (local wrapper) at (1.962, 0, 7.0) m with orientation (0, 0.7071, 0, 0.7071) wxyz (local x to world +z, local y to world -y, local z to world +x); its visible part is four strips of NVIDIA's ReflectiveTape2M5CM_I01 tape (yellow/black stripes) referenced by URL from NVIDIA's content server, lying at x of about 1.968 just in front of the wall and framing an outer 0.30 m (z) x 0.22 m (y), inner 0.24 x 0.16 m rectangle centred at (y, z) = (0, 7.0); its target_region debug surface has purpose 'guide' (not rendered); no collision. Wall slab: kinematic cuboid 0.1 x 2.0 x 2.0 m, centre (2.0, -10.0, 1.0) m, identity, friction 1.0 / 1.0, visual material NVIDIA Concrete_Block.mdl. Isaac Lab's ground plane (z = 0) overlaps the warehouse floor tiles; besides the dome light the warehouse has its own rect lights. No reset events: every instance is identical. AM-Bench's goal_pos observation is the fixed goal (1.77, 0, 7.0). Scene default physics material: friction 1.0 / 1.0, restitution 0.
success: With e the position of ee_link's origin (not the tool tip) and g = (1.77, 0.0, 7.0) m (goal_position; environment origin = world origin), a control step is 'in' when |e_x - g_x| < 0.03 m and sqrt((e_y - g_y)^2 + (e_z - g_z)^2) < 0.08 m. A counter increases by 1 at every 'in' step and is reset to 0 at every step that is not; success when it reaches 100 (success_hold_steps), i.e. at the 100th consecutive 'in' step (100/120 s, about 0.83 s). Orientation, velocity and contact are not tested. g is 0.192 m in front of the marker's origin, so with ee_link level and pointing at the wall the tool-tip point is about 2 cm short of the wall surface. AM-Bench reports inspection_target_held (the success itself) as its only criterion. Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; the 100-step hold above is the only hold requirement. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 20 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 2400 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 2399th step.
goal_fixed: The inspection point is fixed, the same in every instance, and not itself marked in the scene: g = (1.77, 0.0, 7.0) m in world coordinates (z up; the robot starts with base_link at (0, 0, 1.0) facing +x). The success region for ee_link's origin is |x - 1.77| < 0.03 m and sqrt(y^2 + (z - 7.0)^2) < 0.08 m. It lies on the robot's side of the taped rectangle, opposite its centre, a little less than 20 cm from it.
difficulty_note: The inspection point is several metres above the start, in front of a wall, and the end effector has to be kept inside a small region (6 cm deep, 16 cm across) for 100 consecutive steps from a hovering base.
standard_notes: The goal is given as a fixed world point (goal geometry) and ee_link's pose is part of proprioception; the wall, the taped marker and anything in the way are seen only through the onboard cameras, and at the start the marker is far above their field of view (about 56 degrees). Success and the hold counter are not reported during the episode.
